alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring overdue by over a year
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients on a TDF-based backbone regimen. The patient's last creatinine was 478 days ago (2024-10-01, 88 umol/L), and no renal function test has been done since. TDF is associated with chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and Fanconi syndrome, so prolonged unmonitored exposure risks missing declining renal function. The prior value was normal, but a single result from over a year ago cannot confirm current renal safety. Today's plan of routine follow-up with no orders does not include renal monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR today to assess renal function on TDF, and schedule ongoing periodic renal monitoring per guideline.

alerts.title: Annual viral load monitoring now due
alerts.message: Guidelines state adults on ART should have viral load measured 6 months after initiation and then every 6-12 months, or annually thereafter. The patient's last viral load was 113 days ago (2025-10-01, 40 copies/mL, suppressed). Depending on the last test date within the 6-12 month window, the next viral load may be due soon or at this visit under a 12-month schedule. The current plan lists no viral load order. Continued suppression must be documented to detect low-level viremia early, as values above 200 copies/mL carry transmission and treatment failure risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Confirm viral load scheduling; if the 12-month interval has elapsed or is imminent, order viral load testing at this visit.
